advisory.finding: In production, `scan_mcp_clients()` is called with no `cwd`, so it defaults to `Path.cwd()`; `_scan_client` checks `cwd / '.mcp.json'` first (for copilot and claude) and unconditionally returns if that file exists. `.mcp.json` is a generic filename used by many unrelated MCP tools/projects, so running `rebar doctor` from any directory containing an unrelated `.mcp.json` will treat it as the rebar project config and emit false findings (e.g. `KIND_SERVER_ABSENT` when that file declares no `rebar` server), while never falling back to the user-level config.

evidence: src/rebar/_commands/doctor_mcp_client.py:176-184: `if project_path.is_file(): return _scan_path(... scope='project')` — no fallthrough to the user-level scan
New committed files `.mcp.json` and `.codex/config.toml` are now present at the repo root, so doctor run from the checkout scans them
advisory.finding: The project-config branch returns unconditionally when the project file exists, so once a project `.mcp.json`/`.codex/config.toml` is present the home/user-level config is never consulted — even if the project config is malformed, absent a `rebar` entry, or names a legacy variable. When run from within the rebar repo checkout itself the newly committed `.mcp.json` and `.codex/config.toml` will be scanned as the project config, changing what `rebar doctor` reports versus the prior home-only behavior.
